hints.title: Diagonal Inversion Insight
hints.text: With n strings of length n, construct an n-character string by inverting the i-th character of the i-th string.

hints.title: Guaranteeing Disjointness
hints.text: The resulting string differs from nums[i] at position i for every i from 0 to n - 1, guaranteeing it cannot match any given string.

hints.title: Direct Construction
hints.text: Iterate over index i from 0 to n - 1 and append "1" if nums[i][i] == "0" else "0".

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of binary strings (and string length)
complexity.notes: Cantor diagonalization builds a unique string in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N binary strings and checking membership in a hash set takes O(N * 2^N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Diagonal inversion constructs an absent string directly in O(N) without exponential search.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize Cantor diagonalization or use a recursive backtracking / hash set approach.
